prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right lawyer depends on the specifics of your crash (severity of injuries, liability issues, insurance limits, whether the case will likely settle or go to trial), and on what matters most to you (trial experience, communication, price, local reputation).

How to find the right Columbus attorney (quick checklist)
- Experience with car-accident personal injury cases and a proven record of settlements/verdicts.
- Trial experience and a willingness to try the case if needed.
- Contingency-fee agreement (you typically pay only if they recover money).
- Good client reviews, peer ratings (Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers).
- Clean disciplinary record (Ohio Supreme Court attorney search).
- Clear communication and responsiveness (ask about who you’ll deal with day-to-day).
- Locally based — familiarity with Columbus courts, judges, and local medical providers.

Where to look and check credentials
- Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Google and Yelp reviews.
- Ohio Supreme Court attorney directory for licensing/discipline.
- Local court records for verdicts/settlements.
- Ask other lawyers, doctors, or friends for recommendations.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? What were the results?
- What is your trial experience and how often do you try cases?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? (Attorney or paralegal?)
- What are your fees and costs? (Typical contingency is 33%–40% plus expenses.)
- Do you foresee any major problems with my case?
- How long do you expect this will take?
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Immediate steps you should take (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care and keep records.
- Preserve evidence: photos, police report, contact info for witnesses.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other side’s insurer without your lawyer.
- Note: Ohio’s statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is 2 years from the accident (Ohio Rev. Code § 2305.10) — don’t delay.

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short list (3–5) of highly rated Columbus personal injury lawyers who handle car-accident cases, with links, contact info, and recent notable results — tell me your ZIP code and a couple details about the crash (seriousness of injuries, if at fault is disputed, whether the at-fault driver was uninsured/underinsured), and I’ll prepare the list.
